facts: When a rectilinear figure is drawn with one side horizontal, every side is horizontal or vertical. A rotated figure still has right-angle turns, and inward corners have $270^\circ$ interior angles.
When tracing the boundary consistently in one direction, the total rightward length equals the total leftward length.
When tracing the boundary consistently in one direction, the total upward length equals the total downward length.
If the missing side is one **part** of a matching total, **subtract** the known parts from that total.
If the missing side **is** the matching total, **add** the known parts together.
steps: Decide whether the missing side is horizontal or vertical, rotating the figure if needed.
Trace the boundary in one direction. For horizontal lengths, group rightward and leftward travel; for vertical lengths, group upward and downward travel. The two totals are equal.
Subtract to find a missing part, or add to find a missing total.

workedExamples.solution_text:
The bottom is the total of the two horizontal lengths above it.
$x=3+5$
$=8\text{ m}$
The two vertical lengths on the right add to the left side.
$y=6-2$
$=4\text{ m}$

The two upper horizontal lengths add to the bottom length.
$5+x=13$
$x=13-5$
$=8\text{ cm}$

(a) The three horizontal lengths along the bottom add to the top length.
$8+x+10=27$
$x=27-18$
$=9\text{ cm}$
(b) The matching dashes show that the other bottom side is also $8\text{ m}$.
$8+x+8=29$
$x=29-16$
$=13\text{ m}$

Trace the boundary from the bottom-left corner, starting along the bottom to the right. The $9\text{ cm}$ side and $x$ run right; the $4\text{ cm}$ step and $15\text{ cm}$ top run left.
$9+x=4+15$
$x=19-9$
$=10\text{ cm}$

The horizontal lengths give the width of the gap, not its depth.
$24-6-10=8\text{ cm}$
No length is given for the depth of the gap. It could change while the marked lengths stay the same, so $x$ cannot be found.

development.solution_text:
The vertical sides on the right must add to the left-hand side:
$x+\text{right-hand side}=14\text{ cm}$
The right-hand side is not given, so there are two unknown vertical lengths and only one total. The length $x$ cannot be found unless one more vertical length is marked.
